intent: Context, problem, decision, implementation evidence, and what was learned.

register.default: Decision- and implementation-oriented. Prefer concrete constraints, choices, evidence, and trade-offs over a polished retrospective narrative.
avoid: turning project history into a heroic story
retrofitting every decision into an A-versus-B distinction
README language repeated as implementation evidence
generic lessons-learned sections with no decision consequence

evidence_burden.rationale: Project claims are checkable against the repository. A claim about what the code does is verified against the code, not against the README.

source_rules.rationale: A GitHub README states an intention. Treat repository prose as a claim to verify against commits, tests, and behaviour — never as automatically true.

flexibility: Structure follows the project's actual history. Chronology is allowed when chronology explains the decision; sections with nothing behind them are cut.
anti_patterns: Invented project history, dates, or outcomes
Screenshots reproduced without a rights basis
Retrospective certainty about decisions that were guesses at the time
Forcing every decision into the same contrast-and-consequence prose pattern

quality_gates.rationale: Moderate: implementation evidence is often prose about behaviour.

semantic_roles.rationale: Procedure and code carry real structure. A timeline is useful only when chronology explains a decision rather than merely restating prose.
